Markov Chain (S3) Class

Source: R/01_classes.R
MarkovChain.Rd

Construct and validate a finite‐state, discrete‐time Markov chain, represented by an initial distribution vector a and a row‐stochastic transition probability matrix P. Both are validated and coerced to classes StochVec and StochMat.

Usage

new_MarkovChain(a, P)

validate_MarkovChain(x)

MarkovChain(a, P)

is.MarkovChain(x)

# S3 method for class 'MarkovChain'
print(x, digits = getOption("digits"), ...)

new_MarkovChainList(x)

validate_MarkovChainList(x)

MarkovChainList(x)

# S3 method for class 'MarkovChainList'
x[i]

Arguments

a

Numeric vector of initial state probabilities, one per row of P.

P

Square numeric row-stochastic matrix of transition probabilities. See set_state_names() for the default names assigned during construction.

x

An object to check with is.MarkovChain(), a MarkovChain to validate or print, a list of valid chains to construct a MarkovChainList, or a MarkovChainList to subset.

digits

Number of significant digits used to round displayed values. Defaults to getOption("digits").

...

Additional arguments passed to base::print() for the initial distribution and transition matrix.

i

A numeric, character, or logical index for list subsetting. If omitted, all elements are selected.

Value

MarkovChain() returns a list of class "MarkovChain" with elements a and P. is.MarkovChain() returns a single logical value. The print method invisibly returns the validated chain.

MarkovChainList() and its subsetting method return an object of class "MarkovChainList".

Structure

A MarkovChain is a list with two named elements:

a

initial distribution, of class StochVec

P

transition matrix, of class StochMat

Validation

A valid MarkovChain must satisfy:

  • has exactly two elements named "a" and "P"

  • a validates as StochVec

  • P validates as StochMat

  • length(a) equals nrow(P)

  • the names of a and the row and column names of P are identical, in the same order

MarkovChainList

MarkovChainList() constructs a container of multiple MarkovChain objects. All elements must be of class "MarkovChain". Subsetting preserves the class. Subsets containing invalid elements, including NULL from NA or out-of-range indices, are rejected. Empty subsets are allowed.

See also

StochVec(), StochMat(), is.MarkovChain()

Examples

# Choose the transition probability matrix and the initial law of the MC
a <- c(0.5, 0.5, 0)
P <- matrix(c(0.3, 0.7, 0,
              0.6, 0.1, 0.3,
              0.5, 0,   0.5), nrow = 3, ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

# Create a Markov Chain
x <- MarkovChain(a = a, P = P)

# Find Stationary distribution
pi_vec <- stat(x)

# Simulate a single trajectory of length m
m <- 1e4
traj <- sim(m, x)

# Estimate the transition probability matrix
y <- fit(traj)

# Make a list of Markov Chains
L <- MarkovChainList(list(x, y))
L[[1]]
#> Markov Chain
#>   Number of states: 3 
#> 
#>   Initial distribution (a):
#>       1   2   3 
#>     0.5 0.5 0.0 
#> 
#>   Transition matrix (P):
#>         1   2   3
#>     1 0.3 0.7 0.0
#>     2 0.6 0.1 0.3
#>     3 0.5 0.0 0.5
